interpretation_for_paper: Main 2023 stress regime. Broad Q1 scarcity with concentrated £250+ spike activity, strong evening amplification and compound gas/wind/imbalance stress.
Quiet/surplus-leaning regime. Very low spike realization despite some low-wind periods, showing that low wind alone was insufficient to create spikes.
Autumn transition regime with limited spike return after the quiet summer period.
High-wind December regime with low average prices and limited spike activity.
Quiet Q1 regime. Unlike 2023, Q1 2024 did not produce major spike stress.
Extended quiet/surplus period with low upper-tail activity and frequent lower-price conditions.
Late-year transition regime where upper-tail stress began to return.
Main 2024 stress regime. December upper-tail events were physically severe, with low wind and high gas conditions.
Main 2025 upper-tail shock regime. Contains the largest price event and most £300+ periods.
Broad elevated-price regime after January, with meaningful £100+/£150+ stress but limited spike realization.
Transition into surplus/downward-price conditions, with increasing negative-price exposure and weak spike activity.
Mixed-tail regime combining negative-price exposure with renewed £250+/£300+ activity.
Summer surplus-heavy regime, with negative-price frequency and limited extreme spike activity.
Autumn mixed transition regime with both negative-price exposure and renewed upper-tail stress.
Quiet late-year regime, unlike December 2024, with no £250+/£300+ spike realization.
